newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 31.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian national athletics coach Phil King resigned yesterday partly because of disenchantment with the recent Olympic Athlete Program Review. King, the head coach for two years, said he felt thwarted by the Australian Sports Commission bureaucracy, an that business commitments were the overriding factor for his decision. Page 22.

Deposed Australian cricket opener Michael Slater made a rapid 71 runs for New South Wales in a Sheffield Shield match against Victoria at the Melbourne Cricket Ground yesterday. New South Wales were six wickets for 217 at tea in their first innings yesteray after being sent in to bat by Victoria. Page 21.

Defending Australian Baseball League champions Sydney Blues are without a secure play-off place coming into the last round of the regular season. The Blues must win one game in a series against the Gold Coast Cougars, who need to win the series to make the play-offs. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Davis Cup captain John Newcombe has indicated Pat Rafter and Sandon Stolle may play singles tennis in the Cup against defending champions France. Rafter and Stolle are inexperienced at playing for Australia, while Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodfrde are likely to play doubles matches. The tie against France starts in Sydney next Friday. Page 42.

Australian golfer Wayne Grady shot a five-under-par 67 at the A$1.2 million Heineken Classic at the Vines in Perth yesterday to be two shots behind New Zealander Greg Turner. American John Daley shot a 70, Welshman Ian Woosnam had a 72 and South African Enie Els a 73. P.41.

Cyclist Bradley McGee says Australian cycling will face a free fall into oblivion due to internecine disputes unless Australian Cycling Federation president Ray Godkin steps in. McGee, a dual Olympic bronze medallist, was referring to the disputes at the Atlanta Olympics between the road and track programs. Page 40.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League granted North Melbourne a A$75,000 salary cap increase for the 1996 season as merger talks forced the club to re-sign key players. The salary cap allowance was terminated once North won the premiership last year and the salay cap for 1997 is now A$2.9 million. Page C10

West Indies manager Clive Lloyd says future Australian tours should be broken up into separate one-day and Test-match blocks to refresh player squads. Lloyd also wants to be a selector, criticising the selection of the team that lost the Frank Worrell Trophy to Australia in Adelaide. Page C10.

The Australian Football League may host a state-of-origin match at Canberra's Bruce Stadium this June. Two league officials flew to Canberra on Wednesday to discuss the proposal, along with an increase in the number of practice and Ansett Cup matches playd in Canberra. A new stadium was also on the agenda. Page C7.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian swimmer Linley Frame hopes to compete again despite contracting chronic glandular fever. The former world breaststroke champion says she is aiming for the world championships in Perth next year. Page 94.

Australian fast bowler Craig McDermott announced his retirement from cricket yesterday. McDermott cited injury and business commitments as reasons for retirement at a press conference in Brisbane. McDermott is Australia's second most leading wicket taker with 291 wickets from 71 matches. Page 94.

Australian road cycling champion Nick Gates was penalised for five minutes in the Tour of Tasmania for being towed by a scout's motorcycle. Alan Iacuone took the lead from Gates, who was ahead after two stages, on a climb in the race. Gates was then towed by the motorcycle. Page 86.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian captain Laurie Daley has withdrawn from the Australian team in the Super League World Nines tournament in Townsville with a back injury. Ryan Girdler from Penrith replaces Daley, with Brisbane player Alan Langer likely to be captain. Page 104.

Australian swimmer Michael Klim narrowly missed a world record as he won the men's 100m butterfly at the short course World Cup series in Scotland. Klim clocked 52.09s, just 0.02s outside the world record. Klim's victory was his fourth in the meet after wnning the 100m and 200m freestyle, and the 50m butterfly yesterday. Page 99.

Rugby Union second-rower Warwick Waugh hasn't given up hope of making the Australian team's tour of Argentina in November despite having more surgery on a severe shoulder injury. Waugh injured his shoulder in Ireland last year, and may be out for the Super 12 series this year. Page 93.
